content.title: National Cherry Blossom Festival kicks off in the District
content.text: by: Dave Leval Posted: Mar 21, 2026 / 10:21 PM EDT Updated: Mar 26, 2026 / 10:18 AM EDT WASHINGTON (DC News Now) — The National Cherry Blossom Festival is officially underway in Washington following an opening ceremony at the Daughters of the American Revolution Constitution Hall. The annual celebration is scheduled through April 12, and all festival events are free to the public. The festival serves as a major economic driver for the region, generating a local impact of at least $200 million. Last year, the event attracted more than 1.5 million visitors to the nation’s capital. D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser joined Japan’s ambassador to the United States for the opening program at the Daughters of the American Revolution Constitution Hall. The leaders shared messages regarding the ongoing friendship between the two nations. “Where there is in our hearts, there is life,” Bowser said during the ceremony. The kickoff event featured Japanese-themed performances that entertained a capacity crowd at the venue. Some attendees traveled from outside the country to witness the start of the celebration. Laura, a visitor from Toronto, Canada, said the opening ceremonies met her expectations. “The performances were fantastic,” she commented. The festival honors a 1912 gift of 3,000 cherry trees from the city of Tokyo to the United States. To mark the upcoming 250th anniversary of the United States, Japan gifted an additional 250 trees this year. While the festival has begun, the cherry blossoms are still approaching their peak. Peak bloom could occur as early as next weekend. The festival continues daily through April 12. Next year will mark the 100th anniversary of the festival.
